1.sofaString: 388	Pt, ***** ******, is a 16 year-old male with history of cardiomyopathy, s/p heart transplant (**/****), referred by ********* ********, APRN, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.     Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient, patient's mother, ****** ******, and review of the medical records. SW spent approximately 70 minutes of face-to-face time with patient and family. Patient's father was unavailable due to working and current visitor restrictions (*****-19).     Living situation:  **, *****, resides with his mother, and siblings in *** ****** *****, *******. They reside at **** ***** *** ***. * *** ****** *****, ** *****. They **** a 3 bedroom ********. They have one rabbit.      Demographics:  Mother:  ****** ******  ***:  **/**/****  Language: English   Education Level: Associates ******            Employment:  Unemployed/VA Disability                Phone:  ***-***-****     Father:  ****** ******  ***:  **/**/****  Language: English   Education Level: Associate's ******           Employment:  Corrections ******* *** ******* ******          Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  *******- 11  ********- 5     Social History and Support Systems:  ***** lives with his mother and siblings in *** ******, **. He is in the 11th grade attending ******* ******* School/Hospital Homebound. He is unsure if he is on track, classes were supposed to resume this week. He does not appear to have significant motivation to keep up with school and this will likely be an ongoing issue while hospitalized or at home waiting for transplant. ***** enjoys playing video games or basketball with his *******. However, since his last hospital stay he has been unable to tolerate physical activity. ***** reports that he does not enjoy being in the hospital. He does not like being confined to his room and having his sleep constantly interrupted. The changes/restrictions due to *****-19 (visitor policy, etc) are also making this stay more difficult. Having his video games and someone at the hospital with him does help with coping.   ****** and ****** have been married for almost 18 years. However, they recently separated in ******* ** ****. They have not yet filed for divorce and the relationship is amicable. Dad is currently at mom's home with the girls so that she can be here at the hospital. SW inquired about additional family support. Mom's mother and best friend are her main sources of support. Dad also has a lot of family that reside locally to the family and are of support.   Mom is on disability and dad has FMLA/PTO/sick leave and will be able to take time off during and after transplant. Mom will be the primary caregiver post transplant with backup from dad.  Family identifies as ********* and denies any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.     Course of illness:     ***** ****** is a 16 year old male with a history of cardiomyopathy s/p orthotopic heart transplant in 2007, admitted now for antibody-mediated rejection and secondary congestive heart failure, receiving pulse steroids, ATG, and PLEX therapy. His increasing fatigue, fluid retention with declining renal function provoked him to be admitted into the pediatric ***** on */**/**** for further heart failure management with inotropic infusion support with closer monitoring. He also has possible serum sickness with third spacing and migratory arthralgias. Milrinone was weaned off */**/**** but due to worsening renal & liver labs as well as c/o chest pressure/pain was restarted on */**/****. He is being evaluated for heart and kidney transplant.      Financial situation:  Mom receives disability from the VA. The family also receives and adoption subsidy for their youngest child. Dad is employed full time and assist with needs- child support plan has not been worked out at this time. As mom is on disability, caregiving will not result in a loss of income for herself. Dad is eligible for FMLA and has PTO and sick leave.   ***** is covered by CMS ******** Medicaid. Mom was concerned about being found over income at the next renewal period. However, SW explained that with the parents not residing in the same household any longer, she does not have to report dad's income to Medicaid, only child support. SW encouraged mom to reapply for social security disability as well (previously denied due to being over income).     The family has two vehicles. Transportation will not be a barrier for this family.        Family History:  There is a significant family mental health history. Mom reports that ***** was diagnosed with ADHD and *** as a child. He was on medication to treat his ADHD but she reports it was discontinued due to contraindication with transplant. ***** was seeing counselor for approximately 3 years but it ended about 1 year ago. ***** reports that he is not willing to reenter counseling or be on medications at this time. He feels that the *** diagnosis was wrong, he just will not do something he doesn't want to do. Upon chart review, as a young child (elementary age), ***** had significant behavior problems. Notes detail that he was frequently receiving referrals and suspensions due to aggression towards other child. Specifically, threatening to kill others, taking knife to school, punching young girl in stomach hard enough to break a rib, etc.. He was placed in alternative classrooms, *******, and eventually into ******* Virtual School. During that time he also had aggression at home with his parents. He was placed on Strattera, Abilify, and Celexa. However, mom stopped medications due to not seeing significant changes in behavior. Per notes, his behaviors do seem to have improved since starting back in high school.   Mom disclosed that she was ***** Acted for suicide attempt in ********* ** ****. ***** was a witness to attempt and stated that his mom 'scared the crap out of him'. She is currently on medication and is under the care of a counselor and psychiatrist.   Family denies any history of drug abuse or DCF involvement. They also deny any criminal history.      Adherence:  There are significant concerns for adherence. ***** reports that he has gotten better about taking his medications, and taking them on time. SW inquired about the times where he wasn't doing so well or periods of medication missed. He stated that he could not remember when this occurred and could not give SW timeframe of weeks/months/or years ago because he was bad with numbers. There is significant documentation about low levels, parents finding medication around the home, and further evidence of noncompliance. There are no concerns documented recently. ***** now sets an alarm on his phone to remind him to take his medications. The family also fills the pillbox together for the week.      Assessment and recommendations:  Both mom and ***** verbalize that they would like to move forward with transplant. ***** stated that he was tired of feeling like a ** year old. He understands that he will need to take on more responsibility with his care as he is now almost 17. SW discussed the two possibilities of waiting for a transplant: inpatient and outpatient. He understands that the wait will be longer outpatient but verbalized that he needs a break from the hospital. He is most anxious about the surgery part of transplant. SW is also concerned that he does not understand the full extent of what a retransplant would mean for him. He believes that it will 'fix' all of his current problems and he won't be on as many medications as he was placed on after last hospital admission. He denied any need for transplant education. He would greatly benefit from counseling due to significant psych history as well as complex medical condition. He is not on board with that at this time.  **** though recently separated, parents seem to have an amicable relationship. They have done well with *********** ***** and his siblings during these last two lengthy hospital admissions. Mom was very open about her recent suicide attempt and help that she is currently receiving. She is taking weekly breaks from the hospital to help her with self-care. This would be a second transplant for ***** and family and parents are well versed in his care needs.           IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  2     Family Background & Social Support -  2     Financial/Insurance - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 3     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence -3     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process - 2     Health Literacy -  2     Coping Skills - 2     Total:  19 Moderate Risk     The family scores as moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.          Recommendations:  *Require counseling for ***** while awaiting transplant.   *Provide continuing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  *Offer support and guidance to family as needed.
